result.title: MedEvo: Medical Reasoning Evolution through Knowledge Navigation
result.summary: Medical multimodal reasoning models are typically trained on teacher-generated rationales, discarding the valid reasoning in students' own failed trajectories, while general-domain correction methods offer little guidance for errors in image reading, anatomical context, or differential diagnosis. We propose MedEvo, which uses medical knowledge, namely a tag taxonomy and error-type diagnosis, to navigate both trajectory repair and data selection. For each failed rollout, a gold-blind auditor locates the first consequential error and provides a minimal, answer-free hint; the same student retains the valid prefix and regenerates the erroneous suffix. After each round, MedEvo identifies capability gaps across medical tags on a held-out feedback set and prioritizes related questions for new rollouts and repairs. With supervised fine-tuning (SFT) alone, MedEvo raises Qwen3.5-9B mean accuracy across seven benchmarks from 65.57% to 69.12% (47.40% to 54.50% on the multimodal track of MedXpertQA (MedXpertQA-MM)), surpassing teacher-distillation SFT (66.93%). It also raises Qwen3.5-35B and Qwen3.5-397B mean accuracy from 67.91% to 73.04% and from 71.83% to 74.95%, respectively. Our analyses show that failed trajectories contain reasoning worth preserving, that repair success does not imply learning value, and that independent feedback is key to sustained improvement.

AI.brief_summary: MedEvo 面向医学多模态推理，用标签分类与错误类型诊断定位失败轨迹中首个关键错误，保留有效前缀并让同一学生模型重生成错误后缀，再按能力缺口挑选数据迭代；仅用 SFT 即在多个基准上提升准确率，并报告失败轨迹包含可保留的推理、修复成功不等于学习价值等观察。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及「轨迹训练、贡献分配与监督」主线：如何判断轨迹中哪些片段有效、错误由谁引起、监督信号该落在哪一步，可供核查其错误定位与数据选择能否迁移到 latent 推理的信用分配与视觉证据筛选；但该工作为训练期方法，不涉及 latent 状态生成。
